chapter_note: This chapter is predominantly later editorial material — ethical/pastoral teaching about community discipline (righteous anger) structured in a Q&A dialogue frame. The only potential substrate is ¶9, which describes the luminaries' dual function (love/beauty and confrontation/fear) in purifying the soul that passes through the totality. Both sides of this mapping stay within the cosmic system, meeting the substrate diagnostic, but the paragraph serves contextually as cosmic justification for the ethical argument and uses the chapter's 'love/fear' framework rather than technical correspondential vocabulary. Teaching purity = 0.000 confirms minimal substrate presence. The chapter is distinctive for its ethical rather than cosmological focus, with the doctor analogy (hot/cool remedies) as a pedagogical device rather than a correspondential mapping.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic disciple question with 'I beseech you' petition pattern. The question is about community ethics (righteous anger toward obdurate brothers/sisters), not cosmological architecture. High dialogue_frame score (4.3) confirms. 'Brothers and sisters' language points to institutional community context.

Very short (25 words), heavily lacunose continuation of the disciple's question about using anger for righteous judgement. Still part of the question setup — no cosmological content, no substrate markers.

Continuation of disciple's question with stereotyped honorific: 'I beseech you, my master, that you may instruct me.' The substantive question ('whether there is sin for me in this anger') is ethical, not cosmological. Heavily lacunose in second half.

Opens with dialogue_frame attribution ('Then the apostle speaks to that teacher with words of sweetness') followed by institutional/pastoral teaching about righteous anger as community discipline. 'Censure and upbraid that brother,' 'strip him of the obduracy' — community correction language. Institutional score 5.32, dialogue_frame score 4.26. Classified by dominant content layer (institutional); frame attribution is secondary.

Ethical taxonomy of anger: evil anger distinguished from constructive anger. 'Angry in his pride and boastfulness,' 'curses and wishes to humiliate the meek,' 'retaliation and violence against his ill-treated brothers.' All community-context language. No cosmological content. The classification of anger types is applied ethics, not correspondential mapping.

Continues the distinction between anger and 'the strong reprimand that leads to repentance.' Institutional vocabulary (institutional score 4.29): community discipline, 'hard words, in cruelty and harshness.' The renaming device ('its name is the strong reprimand') is a definitional move typical of pastoral teaching.

Doctor analogy — 'you are LIKE a wise doctor.' Pedagogical simile, not correspondential mapping. Hot/cool remedies are analogical, not systematically mapped to cosmic domains. 'Corresponding to the simile' explicitly marks this as analogy. Embedded in the community teaching sequence; the analogy serves the ethical argument about when to use harsh vs. gentle correction.

Extends doctor analogy into the 'two aspects' framework (love and fear). 'The brother in two aspects [...] love, but the other one with fear' — community application. 'Obduracy in one of his brothers [...] foolishness' — community context. Institutional score 3.77 confirms. The love/fear duality is the ethical framework of the chapter, applied to community leadership.

paragraphs.core_text: For the light-givers that are in the heavens shall be revealed with these two aspects, in the aspect of love and the aspect of fear. They display these two aspects of the powers above that are in the heavens, because of their soul that passes through the totality. For in these two appearances, the aspect of love that is beauty and sublimity, together with the other aspect of confrontation that is in them, they shall purify in them the powers above.
paragraphs.temporal_note: HEAVY UNCERTAINTY. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system: light-givers → two aspects → purification → soul passing through totality → powers above. This passes the substrate diagnostic. The luminaries' dual function in purifying trapped light-substance (attractive/beauty mode and confrontational mode) corresponds to known cosmological teaching about the vessels of light. However: (1) teaching purity = 0.000 for the chapter; (2) the 'love and fear' terminology matches the chapter's ethical framework and may be editorially shaped; (3) the connective 'For' links this to the preceding ethical argument as cosmic justification; (4) the paragraph lacks the systematic, enumerated character typical of strong substrate (no five-fold mapping, no metal-body-taste correspondences). This could be pre-compilation cosmological teaching about the luminaries' dual operation, or it could be the editor's own cosmological knowledge deployed to validate the ethical argument. Classified as substrate because no late-layer category fits the content — it is impersonal cosmic process description — but confidence is low.

Direct application to the audience: 'Also, you too, whenever you stand firm in these two aspects' bridges from cosmic teaching (¶9) to individual practice. 'Your treasure will also be for you in that place' echoes Matthew 6:21/Luke 12:34 — Gospel allusion marks this as late material. 'The truth and the watchful teaching' is community-values language. Classic exhortation: moral application of preceding teaching to the audience.

Dialogue closure formula: 'When that teacher heard that lesson, he said: This is truly told, my master.' Stereotyped affirmation pattern marking the end of the Q&A session. Institutional score 6.45 reflects 'teacher' and 'master' terminology. Formulaic session-closing device.
